acceptance.assertion: One canonical source registry defines every released and planned UI locale with canonical tag, native and English display name, direction, status and public page paths; runtime, generators and language controls derive from it rather than duplicating English/German conditionals.

Locale parsing accepts case-insensitive BCP 47 input, emits canonical tags, preserves meaningful script and region subtags and tests exact, language-plus-script, primary-language and default fallbacks with at least pt-BR, zh-Hans, mixed ordered browser preferences and unsupported tags.

Explicit URL or explicit locale surface remains authoritative; otherwise stored manual preference wins, Automatic uses ordered browser languages and English is the neutral default. Query, fragment and discovery state remain preserved and geolocation never influences UI language.

Planned locales are absent from selectable controls, generated alternate links and public locale routing until their complete release gate passes; adding a planned registry entry alone cannot expose a partial interface.

Generated surfaces set canonical html lang, document direction and locale navigation metadata from the registry, including automated and browser coverage proving Arabic-ready right-to-left direction before Arabic can be activated.
Catalogue content-language tags and filters remain independent of the interface locale, preserve valid script and region subtags and are never rewritten merely because the UI language changes.

Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese and Arabic are promoted individually, not as an all-or-nothing batch, and each promotion has complete globe, text, method, proposal, runtime-label, catalogue-localization, metadata and navigation coverage; zero missing keys or untranslated markers; independent language review; keyboard and screen-reader-path review; browser and state-preservation smoke; and exact-head release evidence. Arabic additionally passes right-to-left, focus-order, icon-direction, punctuation and mixed-script review.

Simplified Chinese, Hindi, Indonesian and Japanese remain planned until the first wave and registry architecture are verified. Their internal order is supported by privacy-preserving aggregate visitor, search or contribution-language evidence and available editorial review capacity, without per-user profiling, IP-language inference or location coupling; each locale independently passes the same full release gate.

Machine translation may produce a draft but never counts as final evidence. Safety-relevant proposal guidance, accessibility labels, runtime errors, method text and catalogue presentation receive independent language review before release.

Canonical sources, generated pages, runtime assets, immutable release tree and content-version bindings contain one deterministic locale contract and pass cache-coherence and canonical-inventory checks after every individual promotion.

Every implementation and locale-promotion head passes focused locale tests, full Python and JavaScript validation, desktop/mobile/iPad browser smoke, keyboard and screen-reader-path review, diff-bound self-review, all required GitHub checks and exact-SHA Pages plus production readback before that stage is closed.

approval.note: The user explicitly requested the ideal Commonworld language handling and its implementation. Start only after Commonworld PR #169 is merged or its exact contract is otherwise present on main, and after the active catalog-growth operation and all overlapping leases are terminal. Never mutate foreign worktrees, publish partial translations or infer interface language from geolocation.

goal: Replace Commonworld's English/German-specific locale branching with one canonical registry and then release the planned interface languages one locale at a time: first Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese and Arabic; afterwards Simplified Chinese, Hindi, Indonesian and Japanese in an order justified by aggregate demand and editorial capacity. Preserve the private T033 precedence contract, support script- and region-aware BCP 47 matching, keep content languages independent and expose no locale before its complete translation, review, accessibility, browser, release and production evidence passes.

blocking_preconditions: Commonworld PR #169 merged or equivalent contract present on main
does_not_establish: that any planned language is translated or releasable
permission to expose partial locale surfaces
permission to use IP address, device location or country as a UI-language signal
availability of independent reviewers for every planned language
automatic claim, merge, deployment or production-verification authority

scope for future locale changes that touch additional files

rollback.strategy: Promote locales through separable commits and releases. Revert a failed locale promotion with its generated pages, registry status, runtime labels, catalogue localization and tests together while preserving the verified registry architecture and previously released locales; regenerate and verify the restored exact release.

title: Generalize and release Commonworld interface locales in evidence-bound waves
